question: Should OpenClaw adopt a non-configurable 4-hour cleanup candidate age floor plus the new synthetic-only/protect-main cleanup API as the default cleanup contract?
rationale: The code path is plausibly safer for session state, but it intentionally changes cleanup retention behavior and public cleanup surfaces, so automation should not decide the operator contract alone.

options.title: Accept After Compatibility Repair
options.body: Require the Swift source-compatibility fix and branch refresh, then land the cleanup contract if maintainers want this default safety floor.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Bug
options.body: Keep only targeted stale-transcript/session preservation fixes and defer the global age-floor/API policy to a separate maintainer-owned design.

options.title: Pause Cleanup Policy
options.body: Leave this PR open or close it if maintainers do not want broad cleanup retention semantics changed now.

recommendation.title: Accept After Compatibility Repair
recommendation.body: Require the Swift source-compatibility fix and branch refresh, then land the cleanup contract if maintainers want this default safety floor.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main rollup and Swift protocol model history make this the best available routing candidate for the API compatibility and cleanup-contract decision.
